overview: This file documents U.S. Consul Edward S. Maney’s observance of American Independence Day in colonial Taiwan in 1935 and 1936. His despatches describe official receptions at the American Consulate in Taihoku attended by senior Japanese colonial and military officials, foreign consuls, American residents, businesspeople, and officials’ wives; they also transmit speeches, an invitation, and translations of local newspaper coverage. The materials emphasize ceremonial expressions of Japanese-American friendship, including reciprocal presidential and imperial toasts and the playing of both national anthems, while also recording practical details such as champagne, shared expenses, formal clothing, extreme summer heat, and ice blocks used to cool the consular residence. A final, apparently displaced State Department memorandum recommends sending a copy of an unspecified item to the Red Cross.

subfiles.title: Despatch from Maney on the 1935 Fourth of July observance
subfiles.from: Edward S. Maney, American Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.about: Reports the official reception and afternoon At Home held at the American Consulate in Taihoku for the Fourth of July in 1935.
subfiles.summary: Maney describes the 1935 July Fourth reception with consuls and officials, toasts, anthems, and an afternoon At Home drawing Japanese officials' wives, plus ice blocks and fans used against Taiwan's heat.

subfiles.title: Maney’s response to the Director General’s 1935 congratulatory address
subfiles.to: Director General of Taiwan and assembled guests
subfiles.about: Expresses thanks for the congratulatory address and advocates Japanese-American cooperation, friendship, peace, and social progress.
subfiles.summary: Maney responds that Japan-U.S. cooperation is widely desired, urging focus on relieving poverty and economic security, calling lasting peace essential to social progress.

subfiles.title: Invitation to the Maneys’ 1935 Independence Day At Home
subfiles.from: Edward S. Maney and Mrs. Edward S. Maney
subfiles.about: Invites guests to an afternoon At Home at the American Consulate on Independence Day.
subfiles.summary: Printed invitation announces Consul and Mrs. Maney's At Home at the Taihoku Consulate from four to six o'clock on July 4, 1935, requesting RSVP.

subfiles.title: Newspaper translations on the 1935 Independence Day receptions
subfiles.to: Readers of the Taiwan Nichi Nichi Shimpo
subfiles.about: Reports the official morning reception and afternoon At Home held by the American consul and his wife on July 4, 1935.
subfiles.summary: Translated clippings describe General Terauchi and officials at the morning reception, Hiratsuka's friendship toast and Maney's reply, and ninety guests, many with wives, at the afternoon reception.

subfiles.title: Despatch from Maney on the 1936 Independence Day observance
subfiles.from: Edward S. Maney, American Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Division of Foreign Service Administration
subfiles.about: Reports the official and foreign-community entertainments held in Taihoku for Independence Day in 1936.
subfiles.summary: Maney describes the 1936 observance as a half-hour reception for top officials, consuls, and American men, photographed by the Nichi Nichi Shimpo, followed by a Foreign Club gathering Maney helped fund.

subfiles.title: Maney’s 1936 Independence Day response
subfiles.to: Director General of Taiwan and assembled guests
subfiles.about: Presents Japanese-American friendship as a durable relationship dating from Commodore Perry’s visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Maney thanks guests at the 160th Independence Day anniversary, calling the U.S. one of Japan's oldest friends since Perry, affirming enduring goodwill despite occasional differences.

subfiles.title: Newspaper translation on the 1936 reception at the American Consulate
subfiles.to: Readers of the Taiwan Nichi Nichi Shimpo
subfiles.about: Describes the speeches, translations, toasts, music, and principal participants at the 1936 official reception.
subfiles.summary: Article reports Director General Hiratsuka's toast to the U.S. president and Maney's to the emperor, with translators Koshimura and Matsuo and anthem recordings at the consular residence.

subfiles.title: State Department note recommending transmission to the Red Cross
subfiles.about: Suggests that the Division of Far Eastern Affairs send a copy of an unspecified document to the Red Cross.
subfiles.summary: Brief note recommends sending a copy to the Red Cross, bearing initials and dates from 1935 whose connection to the Independence Day papers is unclear.

interest: Shows the ceremony and material culture of U.S.-Japan goodwill events in colonial Taiwan before worsening relations.
